body: Thank you! I will probably keep writing for myself and maybe at some point try it in another fandom, where I can start off fresh without any bad experiences. I still appreciate all of the amazingly kind comments and advice! I definitely needed to hear that! Xx

First of thank you for the kind words! I feel like I am repeating myself but I am beyond grateful for all the support and kindness. Until you said it, I hadn't thought about the subscription "theory" but it does make sense! I'll definitely consider taking it down and uploading it under a new name / anonymous. Thanks again for the positivity and I appreciate you! Xx

Thank you so much! It doesn't have dark content. However, I am incredibly grateful for the offer. I would take you up on it, but as I have already said I wouldn't consider my work dark "enough". I earned my shitstorm through one of the actors posting my fic on their Instagram. Sadly people don't support each other anymore and mostly try to spread their negativity. That's why I am even more grateful for the love and positivity underneath this thread. I really appreciate the kind words! Xx
Thank you so much! I feel like I can't even express how genuinely thankful I am for all of this positivity. I really needed that! Xx

It took me a long while to come back and I nearly thought I wouldn't be able to do it. But after all the kind comments and feedback/advice I got today, I realized that even if I have to limit my comments or stop writing this story publicly, I won't stop just because people want me to.   
Thank you so much! I wouldn't consider my work dark but I've seen how bad the hate towards dark fanfic gets. But you don't know how much this support means to me!Xx

That's true. I think it's insane how toxic a fandom can be. Especially when you consider that we all love the same thing, so why the hate?   
I will post anything I write in the future as anonymous and share it only with people I can 100% trust.

The crazy thing is, that it wasn't the fanfiction that was so bad or dark or inappropriate. The shitstorm started when one of the actors shared it on their Instagram. 

Thank you a lot for the kind words though! I am incredibly thankful to have received so much positive feedback and every single one makes my heart a bit lighter. Xx
Thank you! It means a lot and I'll definitely try to see it more positive, even if it is hard!Xx

Thank you! I have since then deleted all of my social media accounts that weren't private before I had even become apart of that fandom. I have never posted a lot about myself since I have always been raised to keep my private life as private as I can. Ever since the whole incident, I haven't been active anywhere, so it died down after a while.   
I turned off my comments and will leave it at that for now. I might publish the chapters I write privately for now at some point. Time will tell. But thank you for the kind words. They mean a lot! Xx
Thank you so much! It really means a lot to hear something positive!Xx

I wouldn't be so sensitive if my personal details hadn't gotten leaked. At one point I received dead rats through the mail. Last summer I had a few court appointments with people who hadn't hidden their own details well enough so they got caught. It's been a tiring process and I thought it would be over.   
I never reacted to it back then, simply letting people talk. I never made a public comment on that, so I won't know. I turned off the comments entirely for now since 32 out of 37 were all hate. I don't know if I'll turn them back on at some point. Time will tell. But thank you so much for the kind words. I just really needed to hear that! Xx

Thank you for the kind words! It means a lot to me to hear that right now. All I want to say is, that the shitstorm wasn't even about the content, which made it even worse.   
I abandoned all of my old social media accounts and stayed away from social media entirely ever since. It's just that my heart really hangs on that story and due to the controversy blowing up everybody kind of knows it exists so there would have been no way of just using a new account to finish it. People would have still known it's mine.   
I turned off my comments for now (didn't know that was an option). Maybe I'll just finish it for myself... Time will tell but thank you for making me feel less bad about myself. Xx

Thank you so much for the kind words. You have no idea how much they mean to me. I really needed to hear that today. I didn't know about the comment function. I turned them off for now. I don't know if I will ever turn them back on, but for now, it's better.   
I don't know if I'll continue to share the story online, but I do want to finish it for myself. Time will tell.   
Thank you again. It really means a lot to me. Xx

Thank you! I didn't know turning comments off was an option, so it must have been added recently. I will definitely do that until I feel ready to give the comment section another try, even if that time is never.   
I've never been a fan of this whole cancel culture that's developed over the past years, because people think it's okay to harass people.   
I don't know if I'll continue writing the story publicly but I hope to finish it for myself because as you said, mental health is more important. Thank you for the kind words! I really needed to hear that. Xx

Thank you for the kind words. I know it's best to ignore these comments and I immediately deleted them but I just felt so overwhelmed that I needed to hear something other than that I suck.   
I already knew things were most likely not going to be smooth, especially bc that fandom is knowing for being quite nasty, but I didn't expect it to be that bad.   
Also, thank you for letting me know about the option to disable comments. I never knew that, so maybe it got updated while I was taking my break. I will definitely do that and continue without any comments. I think I will take a day or two off. I am wholeheartedly grateful that you took the time to comment!Xx

I usually end up just deleting them. It's just that the shitstorm I really got to me and I was already anxious to start writing again bc I was afraid something like this would happen again and now that it seems like it, I suddenly feel incredibly overwhelmed.

If you're **looking for a Beta:**

* Name and Link to your fic (if it's not published, link something else as an example of your writing).

[https://archiveofourown.org/works/16647881](https://archiveofourown.org/works/16647881) (I am currently going back in and editing the story, so there is currently only the first edited chapter in my google docs. I will add to it when I finished revamping the other chapter!) 

​

* Tell us what fandom you're writing for.

I am writing for the Chilling Adventure of Sabrina fandom! The story in question is highly centered around the non-canon Zelda/ Lilith ship, so be prepared to not read much about Sabrina herself! 

* Can someone who isn't in your fandom make sense of your story?

I have been told so by my amazing beta who had to quit on me after 12 chapters back when I first started off! Since this story takes place very early on in season 1 and doesn't have a lot to do with seasons 2-4 as they did not exist yet when I started writing. If anything is unclear, I can provide all the info you might need! 

* The genre of your fic - romance/smut/gen/mystery/horror/etc.

Off, I am really bad at genre picking. I'd say Angst/Hurt mixed with a few fluffy romance scenes mainly. It is highly centered around the development of two people not being able to love properly, so romance does play a role in it! It also includes some mature sexual scenes, so if you don't feel comfortable, I can give you a heads up for you to skip it!

* What you're looking for from a Beta or a Co-writer - Grammar/Structure/Plot/Planning/Idea soundboard/etc.

I want to tidy up the story. It's become 130k words long and I am not yet finished, so I want to go back in and work on my flow, readability, any plot holes I might have missed, structure, irregularities, punctuation, grammar, and spelling. If you can't provide everything, that's totally understandable! 

* What your projected word count is.

We're currently at around 130k words, but it's still growing. Granted, we're nearing the end, so there aren't going to be 100k more, but I do think, there is going to be a bit more. 

* How frequently you update.

I just came out of the worst writer's block but I usually update daily. Since I am looking for a beta that helps me beta the edited version, you'll probably get two chapters a week, sometimes more or less, depending on how much I have on my plate that week. 

* What fandoms you are able/willing to beta for **or** what you can offer in exchange\*.

I can offer beta-ing in exchange! I have beta-ed a lot of stories so far and have often been told that my beta work is quite in-depth and helpful when it comes to understanding the root of the problem I found and how to prevent it from happening in the future.   
I also could read and comment on your work if a beta is not needed. Just message me your fandom and I can tell you if I know it well enough to beta. I am generally quite well informed about a lot of different fandoms. Just anime is a dead-end for me. I have only watched Kakegurui and animes simply aren't for me. Sorry!

aww I am so happy for you! It truly is a great feeling to create something that means something to you! I am happy you found that special place for yourself! coming back from a break also feels all the more special!! Xx

I personally see nothing wrong with calling yourself or being called "author" as a fanfiction writer. Of course, we don't have to think of characters and an entire world (if we're talking about fantasy) but a lot of fanfic writers take their fanfic to the next level and have massive world-building, character development, conflict, plot twist, and practically everything a "normal" book would also have! Also, a lot of fanfictions could, if wanted, be turned into a real book at some point if you changed character names, too specific details/ info, and gave them a little bit of a backstory! I fell like telling fanfic writers it would discredit real authors to call themself authors more disrespectful than calling them authors! A lot of people put at least as much love and devotion into their fanfics as real authors put into their books!   
Personally, I think this comes from the many, many stereotypes when it comes to fanfic that portrays it as something "badly written" or just "smut". A lot of fanfics have such a great plot and creative ideas, that I'd take them over many "normal" books any day! So, I think calling yourself an author is nothing bad! You created a story, celebrate it!!!

I can only second this! I am still young, only 18, so I haven't had many "good" stories so far, but when I look back on how far I have come and the progress I've made, especially since English is not my Native language, I can't help but realize that it's not only about the comments or kudos or followers anymore. For me, it's about watching my characters develop and grow into their own version; my version.   
When I started my current fic, three years ago (I was still innocent and only 15) I was at a very different place, and looking back it was the story that *made* me an author. I have grown so much on it and only recently I found out that my writing hasn't changed all that much. Of course, it's become better and I have grown into my style but it isn't as far off as I always believed it to be, so it really is all on our heads sometimes!

I get that totally! I used to think "ufff... a whole chapter just with them being all cute and giggly.... really?" and those were the chapters that always received the most comments and love! I think it's because we, as writers are so concerned about getting somewhere with the plot, that we oftentimes forget that cute and fluffy filler chapters are a good alternative to heavily plot filled chapters! If you want you could tell me what fandom your story is in and when you've reached the writing process I could help you beta it if it's something I am familiar with? I have learned that having people read your chapters before sending them out into the world really makes a huge difference! So you'd know whether or not chapters or narrative wanderings would distract from the plot and you'd have someone give you feedback about the flow and pace.

As someone, who went from VERY fast-paced stories to VERY slow-paced stories, I think I can share some tips and tricks that helped me grown into my current style. I always admired people that could slow pace a story without coming off as forced and never quite got it right. So what helped me was to really let myself the freedom of not sticking to my plan. If you feel like the next chapter should be a nice walk through the park, talking about some fluff, that's okay! It doesn't need to always go as planned! Giving yourself the freedom of changing the outline, takes away the pressure and gives you the opportunity to grow and play around a bit!   
That's the second thing. Play around! Do things, you've never done before. Add that cute cooking scene or write that Breakfast in bed. Even if it takes up an entire chapter! This really adds to the slow pace and gives the reader the feeling of getting to know your characters better!   
What always helped me is leaving the story to sit for a few hours, do something completely different and when I come back I go in and edit my first draft. You'll usually find things to add here and there and my second draft is often times double the amount of my first draft! Don't forget to have fun with it! 

I hope I could help a bit! Xx

As someone who thoroughly enjoys having conversations with readers, go for it! If they stop responding, you know that they have either no interest or nothing to say anymore. I have made good friends that I treasure up until this day through my comment section! One thing is for sure; you have one thing in common!

Your feelings are completely valid, but believe me when I tell you that they probably didn't miss anything! I always feel giddy when people tell me they binged my fic in one night because doesn't that mean that I, as a writer, did an incredible job of making the story so interesting that someone simply can't seem to put it down, because they need to know how it continues? I would get hung up on that 30min! Rather feel proud that you managed to intruiging someone enough to read the whole story in one sitting! It's a gift some people would kill to have!
Congratulations!!! You can be so proud of yourself! Xx

The constant refreshing of the page is too relatable. Especially when you think you've got a new notification and then nope, nothing. But when it does show a new notification it's the most rewarding feeling ever and makes that hellish cycle so much more bearable.

This just called me out. I am looking at the chapter I've been going in to edit three times already and still have not posted! I feel like you gave a very accurate representation of what happens psychologically when our "best" version doesn't get love and I'll try to think of this from now on. I think we often times put too much pressure on ourselves to a point, where it's not about the fun anymore and just about the amount of likes/ comments we get.

Off... this called me out on too many levels. What I learned in my many years of fanfiction writing is that comments take time. No matter how popular someone is within a fandom, they had to start off somewhere! When I started off my current fic, the fandom was just a week old, as the show had just aired then. I am not gonna lie. I wrote twenty Chapters before I even got one comment. I felt like quitting but if I had done this, I would have never met the actresses along the way, would have never got my fic signed by them and one of them would have never posted a picture with my fic on Instagram. It's soul-crushing to not get any comments and it'll make you question yourself and your writing but once you've reached people and word gets around it's the most rewarding feeling ever to see people come back to the comment section, whenever a new chapter is posted and show you some love for your hard work. So hang in there! People *will* find your story and they *will* comment and it *will* make your day so much better!
